summary: A single-shape, config-gated port of a kernel that is proven correct and faster on the same inputs in muse_attention_decode. It does not interact with anything that has landed. The gain is real but small: about 2-4% on sliding decode_1 and roughly +0.3-0.5% on the geomean, which falls inside the CI. So judge it by the sliding decode_1 row and top_kernels, not by the headline.
justification: Mechanism: on sliding decode_1 master runs, after the qkv GEMM, FusedQKNorm, the k and v FP8 casts, store_cache, the q FP8 cast, FA3 (no scheduler_metadata on sliding, so FA3 schedules internally, then runs main and combine) and FusedRMSNormGate. That is about 8-9 serialized graph nodes, and the change collapses them into one 32-CTA launch (1 x 2 x 16). FA3 main alone is 10.2 us of the 145.8 us shape (FINDINGS). The attention problem measured exactly these replaced launches going from 16.56 to 13.12 us, although its baseline already had the fused pre-attention kernel. The I/O mapping checks out against muse_attention_decode/submission.py on master. The qkv row layout (q 16x64, k 2x64, v 2x64, gate 16x64) is identical. decode's qkv is the [1, 2304] contiguous GEMM output, so passing stride(0)=2304 is correct. The positions, cache_loc, seq_lens, page_table, k_scale and v_scale fields have the same names, dtypes and semantics. The caches are [pages, page_size, 2, 64] in both problems. The window is lo = seq - 2047 old keys plus the new key, which equals FA3's (2047, 0). The output is the [T, 1024] bf16 that _gemm(o, dense['o']) expects. inv_freq is built from the same formula as decode's prepare() cos_sin table (theta 500000, arange(0,64,2)/64). Numerically the fused path is finer than master: the query is bf16 rather than E4M3, and the norm-gate is computed on fp32 o before any bf16 rounding. Numbers: the hypothesis quotes 172.8 us for the shape, but that is stale. Master now runs sliding decode_1 at 145.8 us, so 4-8 us would be +2.7-5.5% on the shape. The decode_1 load is 46*145.8 + 16*157.0 = 9219 us-weight, and 4 us there is about 2% of that load, or about 0.33% on the 6-load geomean. That is consistent with the stated direction but below the stated +0.4-0.6%, and well below the ±1.5% CI and the 1.5-2.5% per-shape run drift (LESSONS). Weakest link: the decode_layer finding fused-preattention-triton (neutral) showed that removing the five pre-attention launches did not move sliding decode_1 here. So the claim that the extra pre-attention launches are worth 4-8 us is unsupported. The defensible gain is only the attention-plus-norm-gate part, about 3-3.5 us (+2-2.4% on the shape), which is barely above drift on one row. The run is still readable from the profile: the cutlass flash_fwd row (10.2 us), the FA3 combine, FusedQKNorm, store_cache, the cast kernels and FusedRMSNormGate should disappear from sliding decode_1's top_kernels, replaced by one _sliding_fused_kernel row. That row should be at or below the attention problem's ~9-10 us kernel time.
confounders: None of the four landed hypotheses confounds this change.
fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: gated to window == 0 and batch > 1, so it never runs on sliding decode_1. The new gate is checked before the paired/unpaired branch and returns o before reaching it.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: active at T=1 on the same shape, but it acts on downstream, disjoint kernels (the MoE combine). Every replay starts with a cold L2, so no cache interaction carries across. The effects add.
marlin-block-m-cap-16: inert at T=1 (block_size_m 8 is chosen either way).
sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: T=1 still takes the fp32 F.linear router path, so it is inert for this shape.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is a config-only branch touching exactly one scored shape, and no landed hypothesis acts on that shape's attention block. A gain or a loss is therefore attributable from the sliding decode_1 row's paired ratio together with its top_kernels. Every other row is byte-identical code and works as a drift control: if they move uniformly by +/-2%, that is run drift. A pre-attention-only control (fused attention kernel plus master's FusedQKNorm/store_cache) would not change the decision, because fused-preattention-triton already measured that half as flat here. An ab-revert of any landed item would be uninformative, since none of them overlaps. The headline will be within CI no matter what, so the decision to merge should rest on the sliding decode_1 row being above about +2.5% and the replaced kernels being gone from the profile, not on CI separation.
rules_flags: Query precision: the fused kernel scores with bf16 queries, which is finer than E4M3. The rule only forbids coarser than FP8, and the attention problem passed with this exact code.
Every key: all 2048 window keys are scored for each row (2047 old keys split 16 ways plus the new key from registers). The only masks are the window edge and the causal mask, with no skipping.
Host syncs: none. All branching is on cfg. The torch.empty workspaces (ws_acc, ws_ml, out) are allocations by shape, as master already does.

Module-level caches: _COUNTERS and _INV_FREQ are keyed on config and device only, never on data, so they are allowed. The counters hold no data and the winning program resets them each launch. Two hardening suggestions: build the inv_freq table (and pre-create the B=1/Hkv=2 counters) in prepare() and pass them via state, so nothing is lazily allocated if the first call happens under graph capture. If that is done, assert cfg['rope_theta'] == ROPE_THETA, or key the table on theta. Note that this changes the code relative to the sibling, so keep it minimal. Copying verbatim is also acceptable, since it passed there.

Verbatim copy: copy _sliding_fused_kernel only. Do not import muse_attention_decode/submission.py, which would mean loading foreign modules or its load_inline CUDA extension. Do not carry over the CUDA split-KV extension: it compiles at import (41 s) and is irrelevant here.
open_questions: Scored-submit correctness. The only test that takes the new path is 'batch 1, ctx 10, layer sliding', at the test default page size (probably 64, which the PAGE constexpr handles), plus the scored batch-1 ctx-80000 sliding decode on every timed call. Splits 1..15 are empty at ctx 10 and are masked to -inf partials; the combine gives them weight 0. Can the implementer confirm the attention problem's test list contains the same batch-1 ctx-10 sliding case, so that this exact path is already proven at small ctx?

The hypothesis's 172.8 us baseline and +0.4-0.6% geomean estimate are stale against master's 145.8 us row. Expect about +0.3% on the geomean. Should the harvest classify on the per-shape row rather than the headline? A neutral classification here would be expected even if the change is a real win.

bf16-shape-gated-triton-gemms-small-t (queued) replaces the qkv GEMM at m=1. If it lands first, its output must stay a [1, 2304] bf16 tensor with stride(1)=1, and the gate must pass its actual stride(0). The two changes compose because they touch disjoint kernels on the same shape.

The gate is batch == 1 only. muse_attention_decode later measured the fused kernel at 16 splits on decode_16 as +33% (sliding-fused-triton-decode-batched-deep-splits). Sliding decode_16 and decode_32 are a larger lever here (weight 46 each), and that should be a follow-up hypothesis once this one is proven.
